descs.t: Serbia's Student List has won Sunday's snap election, ending the 12-year rule of pro-Russian strongman Vucic, with record turnout and a projected 140 of 250 seats. We go through the result and how the students got here.

A student-led movement has ousted Vucic in Serbia peacefully, and is projected to win about 140 of 250 seats. Supporters gathered at Slavija Square in Belgrade, and Serbia now waits to learn how the new leaders will govern. We look at the win, what it means for Russia's influence and the tests ahead.

No fires, no looting, record turnout: Serbia's students voted a 12-year strongman out of power. We walk through how a peaceful movement beat a pro-Russian regime at the ballot box, and why every opposition facing a dictatorship should be watching.

intro.plain: Big result out of Serbia. The Student List won Sunday's snap election and ended Vucic's 12 years in power, with record turnout and about 140 of 250 seats projected. Supporters packed Slavija Square in Belgrade. Chat, did you see this coming?

intro.bold: Serbia's students just removed a 12-year strongman, peacefully, at the ballot box. No fires, no looting, record turnout, flags in the streets of Belgrade. That is what people power looks like. Chat, what does Serbia teach every country still living under a regime?

descs.t: Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro, the first candidate since 1985 to win after losing the first round. A day later, Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered Bolsonaro to surrender his passports. We walk through the result, the passport order and what Bolsonaro says he will do next.

Flávio Bolsonaro has abandoned efforts to overturn Brazil's election and says he will sue President Lula for abuse of power instead, after federal police took his passports. Trump said he likes Lula while his own supporters cried foul. We look at what was claimed, what was ordered, and what it means for Brazil's opposition.

Less than a day after Lula da Silva was declared the winner, his defeated rival Flávio Bolsonaro was ordered to hand over his passports and barred from leaving Brazil. Critics call it a stolen election, and Bolsonaro's own camp has now dropped the fight. We lay out the order, the fraud claims and the free speech questions now hanging over Brazil.

intro.plain: Brazil has a result. Lula da Silva won the runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro, and The Economist says no one who lost the first round had done that since 1985. Then, a day later, Bolsonaro says federal police took his passports on a Supreme Court order. So tell me in the chat: is that normal after an election, or a warning sign?
intro.mid: Flávio Bolsonaro won the first round in Brazil and lost the runoff to Lula. Within a day he was ordered to surrender his passports, and now reports say he has dropped his challenge and plans to sue Lula for abuse of power. Trump, meanwhile, says he likes Lula. Chat, what do you make of that: did the opposition give up too fast?
intro.bold: One day. That is how long it took after Lula was declared Brazil's winner for his rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, to be ordered to hand over his passports and barred from leaving the country. His supporters are crying fraud, an adviser says he is terrified, and he has now dropped his challenge. Chat, straight question: would you trust that election?
